ai.description: *Cnemaspis girii* is a small gecko reaching 35 mm SVL. It is brownish-grey with a distinct yellow-spotted vertebral stripe and a prominent black patch on the throat. It lacks enlarged subcaudal scales.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Cnemaspis girii* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, bright yellow or orange patch on the throat, which is absent in most other similar Indian congeners.
ai.habitat: Cnemaspis girii inhabits the rock crevices and boulders of the northern Western Ghats, typically found in moist deciduous forests at elevations between 600 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: Giri’s Day Gecko is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small insects on rock surfaces and tree trunks within its rocky forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Cnemaspis girii* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of two eggs. Breeding occurs throughout the year, with peak activity observed during the monsoon season.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Cnemaspis girii* is endemic to the northern Western Ghats in Maharashtra, India, where it inhabits rocky outcrops at elevations between 600 and 1,200 meters.
